title: More Words ≠ More Clarity

meta.author: Patrick Szot
meta.description: A look back at 10 years of resumes

content:
I've had many different versions of my resume over the last 10 years. When lined up the story might not be obvious to others. But for me, the visualization below is evidence of a career-long struggle and how, with time, I've addressed it. The point is, I've always struggled with presenting myself to employers as a singular talent or skillset. I'm an all-around creative. I write music, do branding, love interior design, art and print design, I have a degree in finance, love professional development and sociology, anthropology, etc. The résumé (as I've fancifully labeled several iterations) has been this important vessel for me, that now tells the story of exploration and then focus, confidence, and clarity.

2013-2017 shows an increase in word count.

I was trying new things, learning a ton, and I put most (if not everything) on the table because I didn't know what would stick. I was in college and working and freelancing all at the same time. I was applying for scholarships and fellowships regularly. These first four resumes got me access to a ton of great academic and professional opportunities; where I continued to throw spaghetti at the wall.

2017 got me into Deloitte Digital and out of the freelance universe. This was the first resume that got me through huge recruiting processes and multiple rounds of interviews. It was also the most full resume.

Between 2017 and 2021 I worked with a ton of clients through my agency and held a couple of lists of resume-like documents capturing which projects I've been on and some of the things I'd been working on or would like to work toward. I got to explore many facets of design without needing to update or apply for other positions.

2020 got me into the world of start-ups. It features a dramatic downturn in the fullness of the page. At this point, I had enough experience to know what I didn't want to do and felt more comfortable leaving experience off the page in pursuit of what I did want.

2023 is speculative.
